column3: Pairs قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ with خَيْرٌ and gives it priority over a harmful gift.
States the decisive contrary pattern: speakers say what they do not do.
Specifies a guarded form of قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا, extending the speech side of the focus.
Its patience-before-response condition only loosely echoes the focus's خَيْرًا لَّهُمْ.
Guidance and taqwa add no distinct route to speech, obedience, or resolve here.
Frames صِدْق through a demand for the promised event, a secondary boundary for f02.
Closely parallels the focus's shift from consultation about ٱلْأَمْر to settled عزم.
Following desire and bad work is only a broad contrary backdrop.
Uses قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا as conduct toward dependent people, extending its social setting.
Names طَاعَةٌ in speech, then exposes a group's contrary hidden planning.
Separates each side's enacted work after rejected communication.
Sets obedience against turning away, but does not develop the speech-to-deed test.
Makes doing what is urged the condition for a result called خَيْرًا لَّهُمْ.
The adjacent call to knowledge and seeking forgiveness lacks the focus's action test.
Treats the authority of an أمر, but not the focus's resolve or truthful fulfillment.
Calls patience and forgiveness عَزْمِ ٱلْأُمُورِ, giving resolve an enacted ethical form.
The immediately preceding card sets the disclosed fighting command and fearful response before 47:21.
Links an أمر to its outcome but supplies no speech, obedience, or truthfulness route.
Joins commanding مَعْرُوف with belief and the focus's better-for-them formulation.
The spoken disavowal turns on what the hearers enact.
Tests capacity for patience after a prior statement, only indirectly related.
The nearest lexical parallel rejects emphatic oaths as a substitute for طَاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ.
The adjacent rejection of what was sent down and nullified works supplies a contrary outcome.
Tests an assertion by producing a book, a limited analogy to صِدْق.
Uses عزم when a relational matter becomes settled, though in a different setting.
Shows heard speech failing to become understanding and responsive conduct in the local passage.
Connects a prior charge, forgetting, and absence of عزم, clarifying resolve as sustained fulfillment.
Combines مَعْرُوف, endurance, and عَزْمِ ٱلْأُمُورِ as an enacted moral sequence.
Its exception for belief and righteous works is too general after stronger speech-deed cards.
Makes صَدَقُوا what was pledged to Allah visible through enduring fulfillment; contrast routing remains boundary evidence.
Contrasts “we heard and disobeyed” with “we heard and obeyed,” and calls the latter better for them.
The nearby following of what angers Allah and loss of works supplies a contrary local outcome.
Its confirmation language concerns revelation continuity, not the focus's commitment-action relation.
Distinguishes those who proved true from liars, without specifying the focus's mode of fulfillment.
The adjacent loss of works is a consequence without a distinct interpretive bridge.
Repeats the timing challenge already covered by 36:48.
Places مَعْرُوف among speech whose value depends on resulting repair or beneficial action.
Directly calls for obedience, but adds little beyond the stronger obedience contrasts.
Keeps مَعْرُوف operative through a settled relational decision, showing it governs action as well as wording.
A prior word and fixed term only faintly resemble an أمر becoming binding.
The recognition language does not clarify قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ or obedience.
Pairs material provision with قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا toward those present at division.
Names patience as belonging to عَزْمِ ٱلْأُمُورِ under hardship.
The local contrast of belief and works with indulgence remains broad.
A questioning use of confirmation does not add to the focus's truthfulness.
Uses مَعْرُوف in a separate marital disposition, without speech or testing.
Marks obedience as conditional by prohibiting obedience to an excessive command.
Defines the truthful through enduring belief and exertion, strongly supporting truth fulfilled beyond profession.
Places صِدْق under testing, a useful but less specific route to f02.
The local testing of reports supports the passage's concern with what claims disclose.
A general obedience imperative is redundant beside more developed obedience cards.
The nearby secret promise of partial obedience to opponents directly contrasts faithful fulfillment of an أمر.
The same surah directly ties obedience to not voiding one's works.
Differentiates messenger and hearer responsibilities, locating obedience in the hearer's carried burden.
A matter being decided offers only a remote parallel to the focus's decisive moment.
Patronage in the local passage adds no distinct evidence for the focus reading.
Confirmation of earlier scripture is not the focus's truthful execution of a commitment.
A pledge bounded by non-disobedience in مَعْرُوف supplies a formal obedience setting.
The local recognition of speech's inclination and of works makes outward signs evidential.
Affirming the day of judgment is a distant form of confirmation, not a speech-deed relation.
Its better/worse judgment about withholding wealth is only lexical proximity.
Uses a tightly concluded أمر, a secondary parallel to the focus's settled matter.
Calls for قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا where vulnerable dependents are at stake, sharpening responsible speech.
The conclusive proof claim does not add a route through obedience or resolved action.
Its contrast between belief and worldly play gives no specific leverage on 47:21.
The ending of companionship after failed patience is only a distant non-fulfillment parallel.
Places obedience within a corrective return when authority is disputed, limiting how an أمر is followed.
The local turning back after guidance gives a contrary continuation of the passage's response problem.
Denial, desire-following, and a settled matter remain too general.
The wish for another return adds no speech, obedience, or truthfulness evidence.
Directly contrasts the profession “we obeyed” with a later group's turning away.
The naming challenge tests knowledge, not the focus's faithful action.
The temporal فَإِذَا construction alone has no interpretive value for the focus.
The local exposure of miserliness and rancor shows a demanded response uncovering interior resistance.
A messenger's announcement does not develop the focus's speech-action relation.
The temporal فَإِذَا construction alone adds no relevant route.
The local warning that remembrance comes too late after arrival gives urgency to the focus's decisive moment.
Boastful speech about wealth does not clarify known-good speech or obedience.
The temporal فَإِذَا construction alone adds no relevant route.
Frames refusal of a competing obedience and sustained striving with the message.
Its call to confirm creation concerns evidential assent rather than faithful fulfillment.
Contrasts formal orientation with a broad pattern of covenant-keeping, patience, and being truthful.
The local call to give, resistance through miserliness, and turning away extend the passage's response contrast.
Shows that misdirected obedience can reverse a prior state, a contrary boundary for طاعة.
Its completed matter and broken promise are too remote from the focus's own sequence.
The garden description supplies no route to speech, obedience, resolve, or truthfulness.
Scriptural confirmation is a different use of تصديق from the focus's truthful response.
The conditional better recompense for belief and taqwa echoes the focus's conditional خير لهم.
Persistent bodily attendance around the object does not interpret 47:21.
The demand for proof of truth is a distant boundary, not support for the focus reading.
Expulsion for a spoken confession does not clarify the focus's speech-to-action test.
The return of matters to Allah is too general despite its أمر language.
Doing good in a legal discussion does not add to the focus's central relation.
Tests a claimed closeness by a demanded consequence, preserving a secondary f02 parallel.
A hostile command supplies no useful connection after stronger command cards.
Verbal acknowledgement is followed by a call to taqwa, but the link to 47:21 remains broad.
The isolated warning about prayer has no available route to the focus.
Questions the absence of prostration, making an omitted act expose a claimed standing.
The messenger's complaint about abandoning the Quran provides a late contrary form of nonresponse to speech.
An easy word during inability preserves relation but lacks the focus's obedience and resolve test.
Directly challenges the gap between saying and doing, the clearest omitted parallel to f01.
Intensifies the blame for saying what is not done, preserving the contrary side of the focus.
Joins قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا to the reform of deeds, directly linking speech and enacted result.
Makes obedience to Allah and the messenger the route by which deeds are set right.
Defines the believers' response when called for judgment as hearing and obeying.
Makes a settled decision by Allah and the messenger binding, closely paralleling فَإِذَا عَزَمَ ٱلْأَمْرُ.
Requires accepting judgment and inwardly yielding to it, an intensified obedience-at-decision parallel.
Preserves the explicit contrary formula سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا.
Recalls a covenant marked by سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا, a direct positive counterpart.
Commands obedience to Allah and the messenger while hearing, directly joining reception and response.
Names those who say “we heard” while not hearing, strongly clarifying empty reception.
Links obedience, fear, and taqwa to success in the same response-to-command sequence.
Treats allegiance as a covenant with Allah and makes its breaking or fulfillment consequential.
Records a pledge to Allah whose promised action is the relevant test.
Shows the contrary outcome when the pledged response is withheld and turning follows.
Names the breach of a promise to Allah and their lying as the continuing consequence.
Commands fulfillment of Allah's covenant and forbids breaking confirmed oaths.
Explicitly connects the truthful with the consequence of their truthfulness.
Commands taqwa and being with the truthful, reinforcing the status of صِدْق.
Contrasts a spoken testimony with Allah's witness that its speakers are liars.
Records a promise of support that is not carried out, a close speech-to-action contrary pattern.
Includes the responsive formula سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا in a broader confession.
Shows aversion when people are called to Allah and the messenger for judgment.
Makes obedience to the messenger consequentially obedience to Allah, without the focus's speech test.
Places obedience to Allah and the messenger within a wider outcome sequence.
Links obedience to Allah and the messenger with a stated consequence.
The imperative to fulfill contracts supports the focus's faithful fulfillment dimension.
Combines obedience to Allah and the messenger with warning, though without speech or resolve.
Commands obedience amid the ordering of a contested matter.
Calls for response to Allah and the messenger when they call, adding a summons-response frame.
Pairs obedience with avoiding dispute and loss of resolve.
Includes obedience to Allah and the messenger in an enacted communal pattern.
Characterizes people by fulfilling Allah's covenant and not breaking the compact.
Makes fulfilling a covenant an accountable obligation.
Characterizes successful people through guarding trusts and covenants.
Repeats the custody of trusts and covenants as an enduring trait.
Frames reciprocal fulfillment through Allah's covenant.
Associates covenant fulfillment and taqwa with divine approval.
Supplies the contrary case of exchanging Allah's covenant and oaths.
Presents a covenantal exchange whose promise is designated true.
Recalls a prior covenant not to turn away, directly relevant to sustained commitment.
Provides the enacted pledge setting immediately associated with divine approval.
Includes good speech to people within an articulated covenantal charge.
Requires justice when speaking, a distinct ethical specification for speech.
Requires an honoring word in a setting of concrete duty toward parents.
Commands the best speech and marks its social consequences, a strong speech-side complement.
Specifies a gentle word within a difficult confrontational command.
Connects excellent speech, calling to Allah, and righteous action.
Commands speech characterized by righteousness and taqwa rather than wrongful consultation.
Names Allah's promise as true, supplying a secondary f02 truthfulness route.
Makes truthfulness beneficial on the day of judgment.
Contrasts a verbal claim of belief with the absence of its inwardly realized state.
Challenges a claimed favor in belief, preserving a boundary around professed commitment.
Shows people leaving a standing address for trade or diversion, a contrary response pattern.
Records a spoken claim of belief that is denied by the verse's characterization.
Contrasts public alignment speech with a different concealed allegiance.
Records a stated willingness to follow that is qualified by their subsequent conduct.
The disobedience consequence adds little after the more direct obedience cards.
Uses sworn claims around a demanded departure, but is less direct than the pledge-break passages.
Records false swearing after hostile speech, a secondary contrary speech-truth case.
Supplies a general contrary image of those who break Allah's covenant.
Its good-word image is suggestive but does not directly test speech by obedience.
Forbids making oaths an instrument of reversal, a secondary boundary for pledged speech.
Gives a mode of calling speech but no distinct obedience or fulfillment test.
Reports a spoken recognition of Allah's true promise alongside an increase in submission.
